overall: Atlanta is actively warming as of 11:30 ET, with the current temperature at 82.4°F and still climbing at a brisk +3.6°F/hr — peak heating is still roughly 3–4 hours away. The warming trajectory from the morning trend (75.2°F at 06:55 → 82.4°F at 11:30) is consistent with a hot summer day building toward the upper 80s.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWP models show notable spread, with GFS and HRRR in tight agreement at 89.4°F versus a more conservative ECMWF at 85.6°F and the NBM blend landing at 87.5°F. max_temp_prediction: Given the 82.4°F observed at 11:30 ET with +3.6°F/hr velocity and 3–4 hours of peak heating remaining, reaching the mid-to-upper 80s is highly probable even accounting for normal velocity deceleration through the afternoon. HRRR and GFS anchoring at 89.4°F carry meaningful weight given their short-range skill, while ECMWF's 85.6°F serves as a soft lower bound; the NBM blend at 87.5°F is a reasonable consensus. A predicted high near 88°F reflects this model weighting with moderate-to-high confidence, contingent on no early afternoon convective interruption — a real but not dominant risk given current conditions.
